title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线不是某个新模型，而是 AI 如何真正嵌进工作：产品故障要被诚实地修复，coding agents 正在把软件推向更多场景，企业采购也开始围绕 agent 重新组织。最值得留意的是，能力增长只是起点，真正的机会在于把它接到数据、流程和现实世界里。

archive.title: 工作流渗透日报
archive.desc: 从 coding agents、AI 服务可靠性到企业采购，今天的 feed 都在指向同一件事：AI 正从单点能力走向真实工作流。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest.

sections.title: From Model Capability to Real Work / 从能力到工作流
sections.desc: 真正的 AI 影响不会只体现在 benchmark 上，而要经过数据准备、流程重构和组织变更，才能抵达用户。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie argues that AI diffusion will take longer than capability progress suggests. The bottleneck is not intelligence alone: companies still have to prepare data, redesign processes, align on new workflows, and wait for the physical world to move. That gap is also the opportunity: builders who connect superintelligence to real operations may create more value than builders who only improve the model.
original:
The way to the reconcile capability level of AI vs. GDP impact is that the diffusion of AI will take much longer than people think. And it will also show up in ways that are hard to measure in GDP immediately.

You could bring the world’s greatest superintelligence to many workflows, and still be bound by the laws of corporate physics: getting data prepared and put into a pipeline, process reengineering and change management, aligning on how the new workflow should function, and so on.

Even after you solve all that, you’re still bound by the speed of the real world: waiting for a customer to respond to a proposal, getting a permit for a project, a drug discovery pipeline taking years to eventually reach the consumer, and so on. Not to mention lots of positive daily AI use-cases are entirely net neutral to GDP, at least in the near term.

AI diffusion is going to be the theme of the next decade. The upside is that there’s a tremendous amount of opportunity in building the bridges between superintelligence and real-world workflows.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 认为，AI 能力的进步会远快于它在经济中的扩散。企业还得准备数据、重做流程、推动变革、对齐新的工作方式，现实世界也有自己的速度。这里恰恰藏着机会：把 superintelligence 接到真实运营环节的团队，可能比只追求模型能力的团队更有价值。
original:
AI 能力与 GDP 影响之间的落差，原因是 AI 的扩散会比人们想象的更慢，而且短期内很多影响很难直接体现在 GDP 里。即使把世界上最强的 superintelligence 放进工作流，企业仍会受制于‘企业物理学’：准备数据、接入 pipeline、重做流程、推动变革、对齐新的工作方式。

解决这些之后，还要受现实世界的速度限制：等待客户回复 proposal、等待项目许可、药物研发多年后才抵达消费者。未来十年会是 AI 扩散的十年，真正的机会在于搭建 superintelligence 与现实工作流之间的桥梁。

rewrite: Aaron Levie expects coding agents to spread far beyond the software teams that first adopted them. Lowering the cost of code makes new categories of tools affordable, from legacy-system upgrades and cyber defense to life-science research and complex data workflows. His contrarian conclusion is that more productive software creation could increase the leverage and demand for engineers, rather than simply eliminate them.
original:
The world is going to be using coding agents for far more than anyone would have thought before. 

We’ll be building tools in all new categories, building software for companies that couldn’t afford it before, using agents to protect systems from cyber risk, automating research in life sciences, processing insane amounts of data in complex workflows, upgrading legacy systems and infrastructures, and hundreds of other use cases.

In short, by lowering the cost of code, we are going to do so much more with it. This will result in software becoming more useful and the leverage of engineers going up dramatically, which coincidentally will mean we need more of them, not fewer.

rewrite: Aaron Levie 预计，coding agents 的使用范围会远超最初的 software team。代码成本下降后，过去负担不起软件的公司、legacy system、网络安全、生命科学研究和复杂数据流程，都可能成为新工具的市场。他的判断也很反直觉：软件生产率提高，可能让工程师的杠杆和需求一起上升，而不是简单地减少工程师。
original:
未来世界会在很多超出此前想象的地方使用 coding agents：创建新类别的工具，为过去负担不起软件的公司开发产品，用 agents 防范 cyber risk，自动化生命科学研究，处理复杂工作流中的海量数据，升级 legacy systems 和基础设施。

降低代码成本后，我们会用代码做更多事，软件会更有用，工程师的杠杆会大幅提升，这反而意味着我们需要更多工程师，而不是更少。

rewrite: Dan Shipper challenges the assumption that automation simply removes human work. Tasks are a useful way to analyze jobs, but tools also create new tasks by changing what people notice, care about, and consider good work. Any serious account of AI's economic impact therefore needs to model work creation, not only the labor that disappears.
original:
this is a very good and well designed report

however, two impt assumptions in it that significantly change the analysis once you start to play with it:

1. the report assumes that jobs can be decomposed into tasks
2. the report models human tasks created by automation always as a fraction of automated tasks. in other words, the underlying assumptions is automation always reduces human labor (or at best leaves it the same)

taken in reverse order:

does automation always reduce human work?
in my experience, the answer is no. automation often creates multiples more work for humans.

...

but if you take it seriously, it shoudl substantially change your perspective automation and jobs

rewrite: Dan Shipper 质疑了一个常见前提：automation 不一定只是减少人的工作。把 job 拆成 tasks 是有用的分析方法，但工具改变了人们注意什么、在乎什么，也会不断创造新的任务。要认真讨论 AI 对就业的影响，就不能只计算消失的劳动，还要计算被创造出来的工作。
original:
这是一份设计得很好、质量很高的报告，但有两个重要假设会显著改变分析：一是它假设 jobs 可以拆解成 tasks；二是它把 automation 创造的人类任务建模为 automated tasks 的一部分，也就是默认 automation 总会减少人力。

但 automation 总会减少 human work 吗？以我的经验，不会。automation 经常会给人类创造出成倍的新工作。如果认真对待这一点，我们对 automation 和 jobs 的看法应该会发生很大变化。

sections.title: The Reliability Layer / 可靠性开始成为产品
sections.desc: AI 产品的竞争不只在新功能，也在于出问题时是否透明、是否真的把用户托住。

rewrite: OpenAI builder Thibault Sottiaux acknowledged that some banked resets did not fully apply in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Affected users will receive another reset and an apology email. It is a small operational update, but a useful reminder that trust in AI products is built in the recovery path, not only in the feature launch.
original: There was a bit of a kerfuffle this morning with some banked resets not fully applying when used in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Everyone who used one in the affected time window is getting another one and an email to apologize.

rewrite: OpenAI builder Thibault Sottiaux 说明，部分用户在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中使用 banked resets 时没有完全生效，受影响用户会收到额外一次 reset 和道歉邮件。看似只是一次运营通知，但它提醒我们：AI 产品的信任感，不只来自发布了什么，也来自出问题后怎么补救。
original: 今天早上有点小状况：部分 banked resets 在 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中使用时没有完全生效。所有在受影响时间段使用过的人都会额外获得一次 reset，并收到道歉邮件。

sections.title: The Agent Distribution Race / Agent 的分发与采购
sections.desc: 当 agent 进入企业采购，平台要解决的不只是能力，还包括发现、付费和责任边界。

rewrite: Claude is turning its Marketplace into a distribution channel for Claude-powered products and agents. Enterprises can use their Anthropic spend commitment to buy products from CrowdStrike, Cursor, Factory, Gamma, and Vercel. The important shift is commercial: the platform is making agent adoption look more like procurement than experimentation.
original:
New on Claude Marketplace: @CrowdStrike, @cursor_ai, @FactoryAI, @GammaApp, and @vercel.

Enterprises can now use their Anthropic spend commitment to buy more Claude-powered products and agents.

Get started: https://t.co/L14yHet6h3 https://t.co/ZdoWCw7th3 https://t.co/zX1HFU1iG2

rewrite: Claude 正在把 Marketplace 做成 Claude-powered products 和 agents 的分发渠道。企业可以直接用 Anthropic 的 spend commitment 采购 CrowdStrike、Cursor、Factory、Gamma 和 Vercel 等产品。重要变化在商业层面：agent 的落地开始更像企业采购，而不只是一次实验。
original: Claude Marketplace 上新增了 CrowdStrike、Cursor、Factory、Gamma 和 Vercel。企业现在可以使用与 Anthropic 的 spend commitment，购买更多由 Claude 驱动的产品和 agents。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger says cloud sessions in OpenClaw are now fast enough to support Remote Terminal, WebVNC, and computer-use CUA. The notable point is not a new model, but the shrinking distance between an agent that can reason and an agent that can operate a remote environment.
original:
Finally got cloud sessions working *fast* in OpenClaw.
Remote Terminal, WebVNC and CUA for computer use.

rewrite: Peter Steinberger 表示，OpenClaw 的 cloud sessions 终于快到可以支持 Remote Terminal、WebVNC 和 computer-use CUA。这里的看点不是又多了一个模型，而是 agent 从‘能推理’到‘能操作远程环境’之间的距离正在缩短。
original: 终于让 OpenClaw 的 cloud sessions 运行得足够快了。现在支持 Remote Terminal、WebVNC 和用于 computer use 的 CUA。

rewrite: Peter Steinberger reports that OpenClaw's Dashboards and Mini-Apps have replaced much of the custom tooling his team built around the system. Their server now organizes work through sidebar entries, dashboards, and plugins. That is a concrete example of an agent platform becoming an internal operating surface, not merely a chat window.
original: Dashboards/Mini-Apps was something I pushed two months ago and now it replaced lots of custom tooling we built around OC. Everything’s a sidebar entry, a dashboard or a plugin now for our team server.

rewrite: Peter Steinberger 说，OpenClaw 的 Dashboards 和 Mini-Apps 已经替代了团队围绕系统搭建的大量 custom tooling。现在他们的 team server 里，几乎所有东西都变成 sidebar entry、dashboard 或 plugin。这是 agent platform 变成内部操作界面的一个具体例子，而不只是聊天窗口。
original: 我两个月前推动的 Dashboards/Mini-Apps，现在已经替代了我们围绕 OC 搭建的大量 custom tooling。如今 team server 里的所有东西都是 sidebar entry、dashboard 或 plugin。

sections.title: Builders Are Testing the Edges / Builder 正在试探边界
sections.desc: 从自我反馈到模型评测，今天的几条信号都在说明：使用 AI 的方法本身，也正在变成一门需要设计的能力。

rewrite: Peter Yang shares a simple stress test for a model's thinking: ask for brutally honest feedback on the blind spots holding you back, using the full context of the prompt. He says Astra's response was especially blunt. The useful idea is to test models on uncomfortable judgment, not only on polished benchmark questions.
original:
My favorite way to test a new model's thinking abilities:

Ask it for brutally honest feedback about your blind spots that are holding you back with this prompt (just paste the whole image into ChatGPT).

Astra's feedback was especially blunt :)

rewrite: Peter Yang 分享了一种简单的 model thinking 压力测试：让模型基于完整 prompt，毫不客气地指出阻碍你的 blind spots。他说 Astra 的反馈尤其直接。这个方法的价值在于，它测试的不是模型能否回答漂亮的 benchmark 题，而是能否做让人不舒服、但可能有用的判断。
original: 我最喜欢的测试新模型 thinking abilities 的方法：让它用这个 prompt， brutally honest 地反馈那些阻碍你的 blind spots（把整张图片直接贴进 ChatGPT）。Astra 的反馈尤其直接。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch is highlighting AI benchmarking as an increasingly important software category. His framing is less about one leaderboard and more about the companies that help the market measure skill, truth, and efficiency. As models become cheaper and more numerous, the measurement layer becomes part of the infrastructure for choosing them.
original:
AI Benchmarks with @Benchmark & @Vercel.

It's ① the most aptly named event in SF history and ② about one of the most important software categories of our generation.

The companies that benchmark models and guide the world towards skill, truth and efficiency.

Join us: https://t.co/9qRlfX4eGO

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 把 AI benchmarking 视为越来越重要的软件类别。他关注的不只是某个 leaderboard，而是那些帮助市场衡量 skill、truth 和 efficiency 的公司。模型越来越便宜、选择越来越多之后，measurement layer 本身就会变成选择模型所需的基础设施。
original: AI Benchmarks with Benchmark 和 Vercel。这是旧金山历史上最名副其实的活动之一，也是我们这一代最重要的软件类别之一：那些为模型做 benchmark、引导世界走向 skill、truth 和 efficiency 的公司。
